A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Grid-World, Basic Control, and MinAtar experiments, including learning curves and cross-environment transfer results in Figures 2–3 and Table 1.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds MuJoCo continuous-control experiments in Section 4.3 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: v3 adds parameterized-policy PMD for continuous actions in Equation (5), implemented using a deep policy network, Adam, and GAE. This is a limited procedural extension; the existing tabular PMD, discrete-action AMPO, mirror-map parameterizations, and evolutionary search mechanisms remain.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds Brax-simulated Hopper, Halfcheetah, and Ant. This substantially extends coverage from discrete-action environments to continuous-action control, while retaining all earlier environments.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain negative entropy and the ℓ2 mirror map. MuJoCo uses the already evaluated negative-entropy comparator. Newly discussed Mirror Learning and algorithm-discovery methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds a complete continuous-control protocol: 256 OpenAI-ES generations on Hopper, followed by evaluation across three environments using 10 million environment steps and 488 PMD updates. Tables 2 and 4 specify the additional training configuration. Existing experimental settings are retained; expanded descriptions of their tuning are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol changes.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds a transfer test: the mirror map learned on Hopper is reused on Halfcheetah and Ant. This extends the existing generalization analysis to continuous control. Earlier error-tracking, policy-distribution, and cross-environment analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 4 introduces an eight-realization reporting setting for MuJoCo. The existing 256-run Grid-World and 100-run discrete-suite reporting remains unchanged. Means and standard-error shading are retained; no new significance-testing procedure or increase in existing run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds learning curves showing higher final mean returns for the Hopper-learned mirror map than negative entropy on all three continuous-control tasks. These are new results under new conditions, not improvements to previously reported scores. Figures 2–3 and every numerical entry in Table 1 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4) gains the missing division by T, and the appendix's summed bound gains a factor T before the optimal value. Appendix C adds a Taylor/Hessian characterization of Bregman divergence. These are local mathematical additions and corrections; Theorem D.4 still lacks averaging, and Appendix A's new drift formula omits the function f introduced in its prose.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion extend the learned-map superiority and transfer claims to continuous control, including transfer from Hopper to other MuJoCo tasks. The central claims about mirror-map choice, evolutionary discovery, and the mismatch between theoretical bounds and empirical performance remain.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly explains the computational tradeoff favoring ES over differentiation through long training trajectories, emphasizing memory constraints and JAX parallelism. Appendix C adds geometric interpretation of Bregman divergence. Existing explanations of estimation error, small policy updates, and possible exploration failures are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation-repository location, previously unspecified tuning details such as Optuna's CmaEsSampler and the 256-task Grid-World selection objective, and MuJoCo hyperparameters, software, hardware, and runtime. This substantially expands reproducibility information; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: New Appendix A explicitly positions the work against automatic RL algorithm discovery, particularly Lu et al. and Jackson et al., contrasting drift penalties with Bregman regularization and discussing differences in theoretical guarantees. Added literature includes Houthooft et al., Kirsch et al., Belousov and Peters, and Jackson et al. (2023), substantially expanding the closest-work comparison.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Method subsections are renamed around PMD and AMPO, limited explanations are expanded, and related-work, geometric, computational-cost, reproducibility, and acknowledgment sections are added. Existing appendices are renumbered rather than replaced.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 4, splits the original combined hyperparameter table into PMD and AMPO tables, incorporates MuJoCo settings, and renumbers the ES table. Figure 1 is resized and wrapped by text, and ICLR styling replaces the preprint layout. Figures 1–3 retain identical artwork.

improvement.justification: Section 4.3 provides useful evidence that learned mirror maps transfer beyond discrete-action tasks, while the repository pointer, fuller tuning disclosure, and closest-work comparison improve reproducibility and contextual understanding. These gains are bounded by mathematical inconsistencies: the averaging correction is not propagated to Theorem D.4, and the new related-work formula omits f. The original empirical evidence is preserved.
